Principles

What every Arabesque Labs interface holds to. When a rule elsewhere in these docs seems to conflict with one of these, these win; when you need an exception, write down why next to the code.

  1. Accessible by default. WCAG 2.2 AA is the floor, not the goal. Every control has a visible label, a visible focus, a 24px target at least, and works from the keyboard. Nothing relies on colour alone.
  2. Bidirectional from the start. English and Arabic, left to right and right to left. Use logical properties (inline-start, not left), isolate numbers, codes and emails, and test both directions before calling a change done.
  3. Semantic roles, not raw values. Components use role tokens (--al-color-text, --al-color-danger), never primitives or hex values, so themes, modes and contrast stay correct in one place.
  4. Say the consequence. Buttons name what they do ("Save name", not "OK"). Before an action, say what it will touch; during it, show it's working; after it, say what happened.
  5. Fewest steps. Ask only what's needed, in the order people think of it. Don't make people confirm what they can undo.
  6. Reversible where possible. Do reversible actions at once, with Undo. Ask first only for what can't be undone, and say why.
  7. Never lose work. Keep what was typed through errors, failed saves, language switches and dialogs closing.
  8. Honest states. Show "Saved" only when the current value is saved; mark a figure as stale while it's worked out again; never show success before it's true.

Scope

This system covers tokens, CSS components, optional JavaScript helpers and the patterns in patterns.md. It doesn't cover product copy, pricing, legal text or business rules; those come from the product.
